title: Counters in Function Block Diagram: count parts to a batch
summary: Edit a Function Block Diagram so that a CTU counter counts three parts, lights BatchFull, and clears with Reset.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real photocell bounces or how fast a real line can be counted.
objectives: Read a counter in a Function Block Diagram as a block with a memory: an instance whose input ports receive connections and whose outputs Q and CV can be connected on.
Make a CTU count rising edges up to its preset, and clear it with a reset input.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/BatchCount.fbd.json the counter block Count (CTU), the constant 3 on its PV and the output BatchFull are placed, and Q is already connected to BatchFull. Nothing reaches CU or R. Make BatchFull light when the third part has been counted and go out when Reset is pressed.
stages.checkpoint: You can say what each input port of a CTU does, and what an input port with no connection receives.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Predict BatchFull at {{t:50}} ms (two parts counted), at {{t:60}} ms (the third part arrives) and at {{t:80}} ms (Reset is pressed). The first part stays in front of the sensor for several scans.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:BatchCount.BatchFull=false@50|OFF}} at {{t:50}} ms, because a part counts once however long it stays; {{v:BatchCount.BatchFull=true@60|ON}} at {{t:60}} ms; {{v:BatchCount.BatchFull=false@80|OFF}} at {{t:80}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting diagram, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starter has the counter and the preset, but PartSensor and Reset are not connected to it, so Count never counts and BatchFull stays OFF. Change the diagram so that each part in front of PartSensor counts once, BatchFull lights at the third, and Reset clears the count. Do not change the constant 3 or the connection to BatchFull.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named BatchCount and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:30}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:60}} ms: nothing happens when the first part leaves, BatchFull rises at {{t:60}} ms, and a new part at {{t:100}} ms does not light it again.
stages.checkpoint: BatchFull rises once at {{t:60}} ms and falls once at {{t:80}} ms; one part after Reset leaves it OFF at {{t:110}} ms.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: What does the counter count, the level of PartSensor or its rising edge? Then imagine PartSensor connected to R and Reset to CU: what would BatchFull do in this scenario?
stages.checkpoint: CTU counts rising edges, so the first part counts once although it stays in front of the sensor for {{t:20}} ms. With the two connections swapped, each part would clear the count and only Reset would count, so BatchFull would never light.

hints.text: Look at the input ports of Count that have no connection, and at the two input blocks whose OUT reaches nothing.
Draw a connection from PartSensor.OUT to Count.CU, and another from Reset.OUT to Count.R. Do not change the constant 3 or the connection to BatchFull.

faultCases: The starter has the counter and the preset, but PartSensor and Reset are not connected to it, so Count never counts and BatchFull stays OFF.
